title: How Sam Parr Builds Businesses: deal climbing, pricing, focus and zero friction
summary: Sam Parr traces his climb from $10 hot dogs to the Hustle's sale to HubSpot, showing how each larger deal came from delivering more value. He covers copywriting, pricing mistakes, selling to early advertisers, negotiating an acquisition, staying focused, and cutting friction when starting.

principles.text: Price by value delivered: you take a small fraction of the value, so higher-value offers justify higher prices.
principles.quote: it's all about value given so the value you get from one meal isn't significant the value that you get from finding a place to live is quite high

principles.text: Copywriting is the most important skill: understand what motivates people and use it to persuade them.
principles.quote: copywriting is the most important skill not only in business but life

principles.text: Avoid the $299 no-man's-land price. Go clearly cheap (impulse buy) or much higher, since buyers at $299 would pay far more.
principles.quote: i should have charged either 99 or 2 000 3.99 or 299 is no man's land

principles.text: Pre-sell with a simple document and strong copy before building. Trends took $50K in pre-sales from a Word doc.
principles.quote: we actually had fifty thousand dollars in pre-sales just from like a word document that explained what it was

principles.text: In an acquisition conversation, surface all your flaws up front to flush out dealbreakers fast and remove their later leverage.
principles.quote: i'm going to email you a list of all the reasons why you shouldn't buy us and if any of those are red flags we can continue talking

principles.text: Small companies beat big ones on speed and focus. Pick one metric, review it weekly, and say no to everything else.
principles.quote: small companies we really only have two advantages over big companies which is speed and focus
